title: Master Guide to Indian Geography for Banking & Competitive Exams

river_systems.origin: Bokhar Chu glacier near Lake Manasarovar in Tibet (known as Singi Khamban / Lion's Mouth)

tributaries.name: Jhelum (Vitasta)
tributaries.origin: Verinag spring in Jammu & Kashmir; flows into Wular Lake

tributaries.name: Chenab (Asikni)
tributaries.origin: Chandra and Bhaga streams near Bara Lacha La pass in Himachal Pradesh (Largest tributary of Indus)

tributaries.name: Ravi (Purushni)
tributaries.origin: Kullu hills near Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh

tributaries.name: Beas (Vipasa)
tributaries.origin: Beas Kund near Rohtang Pass (entirely within India, joins Sutlej at Harike)

tributaries.name: Sutlej (Shutudri)
tributaries.origin: Rakas Lake near Manasarovar in Tibet (known as Langqen Zangbo; enters India via Shipki La pass)

river_systems.treaty: Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) 1960 signed in Karachi by PM Jawaharlal Nehru and President Ayub Khan, brokered by World Bank. India controls Eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej), Pakistan controls Western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab).

river_systems.origin: Originates as Bhagirathi from Gangotri Glacier (Gaumukh) in Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand. Confluence of Bhagirathi and Alaknanda at Devprayag forms the Ganga.

tributaries.name: Yamuna
tributaries.origin: Yamunotri Glacier on Bandarpoonch peak. Merges at Prayagraj (Triveni Sangam). Major tributaries: Chambal, Betwa, Ken, Tons

tributaries.name: Ramganga
tributaries.origin: Garhwal hills; flows through Jim Corbett National Park

tributaries.name: Gomti
tributaries.origin: Gomat Taal (Fulhar Jheel) in Pilibhit, UP (only major Ganga tributary originating in plains)

tributaries.name: Ghaghara (Karnali)
tributaries.type: Left-bank tributary (Largest tributary by volume of water)

tributaries.name: Gandak
tributaries.origin: Nepal Himalayas near Dhaulagiri and Mt Everest

tributaries.name: Kosi
tributaries.type: Left-bank tributary ('Sorrow of Bihar' due to frequent course shifts)

river_systems.origin: Chemayungdung Glacier near Lake Manasarovar in Tibet (known as Tsangpo)
river_systems.entry_into_india: Enters Arunachal Pradesh through Great Bend near Namcha Barwa as 'Siang' or 'Dihang'
river_systems.tributaries: Subansiri (largest), Dibang, Lohit (Dhola-Sadiya / Bhupen Hazarika Bridge over Lohit is 9.15 km long), Manas, Sankosh, Teesta
river_systems.key_features: Forms Majuli Island (Assam) - world's largest inhabited freshwater river island. In Bangladesh, joined by Teesta and called Jamuna; merges with Padma (Ganga) and Meghna to form Sundarbans Delta into Bay of Bengal.

east_flowing.length: 1,465 km (Second longest river in India and longest in Peninsular India)
east_flowing.origin: Trimbakeshwar near Nashik, Maharashtra. Tributaries: Penganga, Wainganga, Wardha, Pranhita, Indravati, Manjira
Mahabaleshwar in Western Ghats (Maharashtra). Tributaries: Tungabhadra, Koyna, Bhima, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Musi (Hyderabad located on Musi)
Dhamtari district in Dandakaranya, Chhattisgarh. Flows through Odisha; Hirakud Dam built across it. Tributaries: Seonath, Hasdeo, Mand, Ib, Tel

Talakaveri in Brahmagiri range, Kodagu (Coorg), Karnataka. Known as 'Ganga of the South'. Shivasamudram Falls (first hydro-electric station in India, 1902). Tributaries: Harangi, Hemavati, Arkavathi, Kabini, Bhavani, Amaravati

west_flowing_rift_valley.origin: Amarkantak Plateau, Anuppur, Madhya Pradesh. Flows in a rift valley between Vindhya range (north) and Satpura range (south). Dhuandhar Falls (Marble Rocks, Jabalpur). Sardar Sarovar Dam.
Multai in Betul district, Madhya Pradesh. Flows through rift valley south of Satpura range into Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea). Ukai Dam built on it.

west_flowing_rift_valley.significance: Only river in India that cuts the Tropic of Cancer twice (in MP and Gujarat).
Inland drainage river originating near Pushkar (Aravalli range), disappears into the Rann of Kutch.

major_dams_and_projects.facts: Highest dam in India (height: 260.5 meters). World's 4th tallest rock and earth-fill embankment dam.
Longest earthen dam in India and the world (total length: 25.8 km; main dam: 4.8 km). Built in 1957.
Second tallest gravity dam in India (height: 226 meters). Creates the Gobind Sagar reservoir.
Terminal dam on Narmada; Statue of Unity (world's tallest statue, 182 m, dedicated to Sardar Patel) located 3.2 km downstream on Sadhu Bet island.
World's largest masonry dam built with stone masonry instead of concrete.
One of the highest arch dams in Asia, constructed between two granite hills (Kuravan and Kurathi).
One of the oldest multipurpose dams in India (completed 1934).
Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar is the largest artificial man-made reservoir in India by surface area.

mountain_peaks.facts: Highest mountain peak in India (under undisputed Indian territory). World's third highest peak. UNESCO Mixed World Heritage Site.
Second highest peak in the world.
Second highest peak in India located entirely within Indian territory. Biosphere Reserve.
Highest mountain peak in South India, Western Ghats, and Peninsular India. Known as 'Everest of South India'.
Second highest peak in South India; highest point in Nilgiris at the junction of Western and Eastern Ghats.
Highest peak of the Aravalli Range (the oldest fold mountain system in India).
Highest point in Madhya Pradesh and the Satpura Range.
Highest peak of the Eastern Ghats.

mountain_passes.connects: Kullu Valley with Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh
mountain_passes.facts: Atal Tunnel (9.02 km, world's longest highway tunnel above 10,000 feet) built under Rohtang Pass
Sutlej River enters India through this pass
Ancient Silk Route trade pass reopened in 2006
Crucial route for Kailash Mansarovar Yatra
Major low mountain pass in Western Ghats breaking Nilgiri and Anamalai hills
